## 6. Supervised Task 1 – Regression

### 6.1 Define Features & Target

Pick your regression target and features (these must match what you implemented in `ds.py`):

```{python}
reg_feature_cols = [
    # "feature_1",
    # "feature_2",
    # ...
]

reg_target_col = "your_regression_target"

X_reg, y_reg = ds.prepare_features_and_target(
    df_fe,
    feature_cols=reg_feature_cols,
    target_col=reg_target_col,
)

X_reg.shape, y_reg.shape
```

### 6.2 Train/Test Split

```{python}
X_train_reg, X_test_reg, y_train_reg, y_test_reg = ds.split_train_test(
    X_reg,
    y_reg,
    test_size=0.2,
    stratify=False,  # regression: keep False
    random_state=ds.RANDOM_STATE,
)
```

### 6.3 Train Model & Evaluate

You can either use the **full workflow**:

```{python}
reg_result = ds.full_regression_workflow(
    df=df_fe,
    feature_cols=reg_feature_cols,
    target_col=reg_target_col,
    test_size=0.2,
    random_state=ds.RANDOM_STATE,
)

reg_result["metrics"]
```

Or call the pieces manually:

```{python}
# Manual version (uncomment if not using full_regression_workflow)
# model_reg = ds.train_regression_model(X_train_reg, y_train_reg)
# y_pred_reg = ds.predict_regression(model_reg, X_test_reg)
# reg_metrics = ds.regression_metrics(y_test_reg, y_pred_reg)
# reg_metrics
```

### 6.4 Visualize & Interpret

```{python}
y_test = reg_result["y_test"]
y_pred = reg_result["y_pred"]

plt.figure()
plt.scatter(y_test, y_pred, alpha=0.7)
plt.xlabel("True values")
plt.ylabel("Predicted values")
plt.title("Regression: True vs Predicted")
plt.plot([y_test.min(), y_test.max()],
         [y_test.min(), y_test.max()],
         linestyle="--")
plt.show()
```

In text:

* Are predictions systematically biased (over/under-prediction)?
* Is the R² meaningful in this context?
* Are there data regions where the model does particularly poorly?

## 7. Supervised Task 2 – Classification (If Applicable)

If your project includes classification:

### 7.1 Define Features & Target

```{python}
clf_feature_cols = [
    # "feature_1",
    # "feature_2",
    # ...
]

clf_target_col = "your_classification_target"

X_clf, y_clf = ds.prepare_features_and_target(
    df_fe,
    feature_cols=clf_feature_cols,
    target_col=clf_target_col,
)
```

### 7.2 Train/Test Split (With Stratification)

```{python}
X_train_clf, X_test_clf, y_train_clf, y_test_clf = ds.split_train_test(
    X_clf,
    y_clf,
    test_size=0.2,
    stratify=True,
    random_state=ds.RANDOM_STATE,
)
```

### 7.3 Train Model & Evaluate

```{python}
clf_model = ds.train_classification_model(X_train_clf, y_train_clf)
y_pred_clf = ds.predict_classification(clf_model, X_test_clf)

clf_metrics = ds.classification_metrics(y_test_clf, y_pred_clf)
clf_metrics
```

In text:

* Is accuracy alone sufficient in your context?
* How do your metrics look across classes (if imbalanced)?
* Could misclassification have ethical or practical consequences?

## 8. Unsupervised Task – Clustering (If Applicable)

### 8.1 Select Features for Clustering

```{python}
cluster_feature_cols = [
    # "feature_1",
    # "feature_2",
    # ...
]

X_cluster = df_fe[cluster_feature_cols].dropna()
X_cluster.shape
```

### 8.2 Run Clustering

Pick a reasonable cluster count (justify in your report):

```{python}
n_clusters = 3  # or your chosen K

cluster_labels = ds.run_clustering_model(
    X_cluster,
    n_clusters=n_clusters,
    random_state=ds.RANDOM_STATE,
)

cluster_metrics = ds.clustering_metrics(X_cluster, cluster_labels)
cluster_metrics
```

### 8.3 Visualize & Interpret

For 2D or 3D subsets of features:

```{python}
X_plot = X_cluster.iloc[:, :2].copy()
X_plot["cluster"] = cluster_labels

sns.scatterplot(
    data=X_plot,
    x=X_plot.columns[0],
    y=X_plot.columns[1],
    hue="cluster",
    palette="tab10"
)
plt.title("Clustering: Feature Space")
plt.show()
```

In text:

* Do clusters correspond to meaningful groups?
* Are there any surprising combinations?
* How stable or fragile do the clusters seem?
